scope: November Maths school mock: AQA AS/Year 1 Pure only; Statistics, Mechanics, radians and Year 2 calculus excluded.
motivation: v161 confirmed 121 in-scope Pure questions; substantive weaker areas included 5 differentiation, 3 trigonometry, 5 explicitly categorised Transformations and only two direct binomial practice items. Multi-part practice is preferable to further near-identical two-mark questions.

questions.prompt: Let f(x)=x²−4x+1 and g(x)=−2f(x−3)+5. Write f in completed-square form. Describe the transformations from y=f(x) to y=g(x), and hence find the turning point of g. Find the image on g of the point (0,1) on f.
markPoints: The turning point of f is (2,−3).
Replacing x with x−3 translates the graph 3 units right.
Multiplication by −2 reflects in the x-axis and stretches vertically by factor 2.
Adding 5 translates the graph 5 units upwards.

questions.prompt: Solve 2cos²θ+3sinθ−3=0 for 0°≤θ<360°. Show why all solutions have been found.
markPoints: All solutions in the given interval are θ=30°, 90°, 150°.

questions.prompt: The curve C has equation y=x³−6x²+9x+2. Find both stationary points and determine their nature. Find the equation of the tangent to C at x=0.
markPoints: At x=1, y=6; at x=3, y=2.
At x=1 the second derivative is negative (local maximum); at x=3 it is positive (local minimum).
At x=0 the gradient is dy/dx=9 and the point is (0,2).

questions.prompt: Expand (2−3x)⁵ up to and including the term in x³. Hence estimate 1.97⁵ by taking x=0.01. Explain why this is only an approximation.
markPoints: The coefficients of the first four binomial terms are 1, 5, 10 and 10.
The terms in x⁴ and x⁵ have been omitted; the value is therefore approximate.

questions.subtopic: Signed integral and total enclosed area
questions.prompt: The curve y=x²−4 is considered between x=−3 and x=3. Calculate the signed definite integral over this interval and the total geometric area between the curve and the x-axis. Give exact answers.
markPoints: The curve crosses the x-axis at x=−2 and x=2.
The signed integral from −3 to 3 equals −6.
The geometric area must be split at −2 and 2, reversing the sign for the region below the axis.
The region below the axis has area ∫(from −2 to 2)(4−x²) dx=32/3.
Each outer region has area ∫(from 2 to 3)(x²−4) dx=7/3, by symmetry.
The total geometric area is 32/3+2(7/3)=46/3 square units.

questions.subtopic: Inverse function, range and restricted domain
questions.prompt: The function f is defined by f(x)=(2x+3)/(x−1), for x>1. Rewrite f in the form a+b/(x−1). Explain why f is one-to-one, state its range, and obtain a formula for f⁻¹(x) with its domain. Evaluate f⁻¹(7).
markPoints: For x>1, the reciprocal term 5/(x−1) strictly decreases as x increases, so f is one-to-one.
As x→1+ the output tends to +∞, and as x→∞ it approaches 2 from above.

questions.prompt: A circle has equation (x−2)²+(y+1)²=20. The point P=(6,1) lies on the circle. Find the tangent at P. The horizontal line y=1 meets the circle at P and Q; find Q and the length PQ.
markPoints: The circle has centre (2,−1) and radius √20.
The radius from the centre to P has gradient 2/4=1/2.
The tangent has gradient −2 because it is perpendicular to the radius.
Use point-gradient form y−1=−2(x−6), giving y=−2x+13.
Set y=1 in the circle: (x−2)²+4=20, giving x=6 or x=−2, so Q=(−2,1).

questions.prompt: Let f(x)=2x³−5x²−4x+3. Show that x−3 is a factor, then factorise f(x) completely. Hence solve f(x)<0.
markPoints: By the factor theorem x−3 is a factor.
Use a sign table or test values to identify the negative intervals.
